html:
Olzhas Suleimenov (born 1936) is a Kazakh poet who writes in Russian, and the founder in 1989 of the Nevada-Semipalatinsk movement, which helped end Soviet nuclear testing in Kazakhstan.

Trained as a geologist, he became famous in 1961 with a poem written for Yuri Gagarin's flight into space. His book Az i Ya (1975) read the medieval Russian Tale of Igor's Campaign as full of Turkic words and influence, and argued for the steppe peoples' place in Russian history. Soviet critics attacked it and it was withdrawn.

In February 1989, after reports of radiation leaking from a test, he spoke out on Kazakh television and called a public meeting in Almaty. It launched the Nevada-Semipalatinsk movement, named in solidarity with protesters at the American test site in Nevada, which gathered more than a million signatures. The last Soviet test at the Semipalatinsk test site came that October, and in 1991 Nursultan Nazarbayev closed it for good. Suleimenov later served as Kazakhstan's ambassador to Italy and to UNESCO.
